topIssues.title: [Flake] op-e2e-fuzz: 'Too long with no output (15m)' — parallel buffers fuzz output until job completion
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Filed by Claude (AI assistant) on behalf of Adrian Sutton.

## Summary

The `op-e2e-fuzz` CircleCI job intermittently fails with:

```
Too long with no output (exceeded 15m0s): context deadline exceeded
```

The `Fuzz` step is killed by CircleCI's `no_output_timeout: 15m` before producing any output.

## Evidence

- Failing run: https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/127181/workflows/3f6b0990-218b-47ef-9826-bd2df41f008f/jobs/5158358 (job `5158358`)
- Step log (entire output before the kill):
  ```
  parallel --tag -N1 "go test -run NOTAREALTEST -tags cgo_test -v -fuzztime 10s -fuzz {} ./opgeth" ::: FuzzFjordCostFunction FuzzFastLzGethSolidity FuzzFastLzCgo
  error: Recipe `fuzz` failed on line 72 with exit code 255
  Too long with no output (exceeded 15m0s): context deadline exceeded
  ```
- Frequency (CircleCI Insights, `main` workflow): **3 failures / 733 runs (~99.6% success)**.
- Job duration profile: median 395s, **p95 824s (~14m)**, max 1476s (~24m) — routinely runs close to the 15-minute no-output timeout.

## Likely Mechanism

`op-e2e/justfile` runs the three fuzz targets under GNU `parallel --tag` (line 72). `parallel` defaults to `--group`, which **buffers each job's output and only flushes it when that job completes**. CircleCI's `no_output_timeout` therefore measures the gap between job completions, not actual test progress.

`FuzzFjordCostFunction` spins up a full op-geth system (`NewOpGeth`) in *every* fuzzing worker process. Under CPU contention on the shared CI box this setup is slow and is not bounded by the test's 60s context (`gethNode.Node.Start()` is not ctx-bounded). When `FuzzFjordCostFunction` finishes more than 15 minutes after the two fast targets, there is a >15-minute window with no output and CircleCI kills the step — even though the test is still making progress.

## Affected
- Package: `op-e2e/opgeth` (`github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/op-e2e/opgeth`)
- Recipe: `op-e2e/justfile` `fuzz`
- CI job: `op-e2e-fuzz`

A fix PR is in progress. Root cause and fix will be validated by reproduction before the PR is opened.

topIssues.title: op-conductor: gracefully recover from interop reorgs
topIssues.author: karlfloersch
topIssues.body:
## Problem

When an interop cross-chain validation detects an invalid executing message and triggers a reorg, the EL is rewound to the last common ancestor (potentially hundreds or thousands of blocks behind the tip). After this rewind, op-conductor's health check compares the unsafe head timestamp to wall clock time, finds the sequencer far behind, declares it unhealthy, and calls `admin_stopSequencer`. With sequencing stopped, the unsafe head can never advance, creating a **permanent deadlock** that requires manual intervention (restarting the op-node pod).

This means every interop reorg currently requires manual recovery of the sequencer.

## Mechanism

1. Supernode interop activity detects an invalid executing message at block N
2. The invalid block is replaced with a deposit-only block; supernode reports the corrected safe head
3. Sequencer EL receives the forkchoice update, detects chain divergence at block N, and rewinds from the tip to block N-1
4. The unsafe head is now far behind wall clock (e.g. 1400+ seconds behind after a rewind of ~1500 blocks)
5. Conductor health check fires, sees the stale unsafe head, declares the sequencer unhealthy
6. Conductor calls `admin_stopSequencer` — the sequencer can no longer produce blocks
7. Since blocks can't be produced, the unsafe head never catches up — **circular deadlock**

## Expected Behavior

The conductor should recognize that an EL rewind (reorg) is a transient event and allow the sequencer to recover by continuing to produce blocks from the rewound head. The sequencer will naturally catch up to the tip as it sequences new blocks.

## Possible Solution Direction

The right fix isn't fully determined yet, but one promising direction:

**Conductor queries the consensus layer (via consensus-layer HA) for safe chain state.** The conductor already participates in HA, so it could leverage the consensus layer to access safe head, cross-safe head, and local-safe head information. With this data, the conductor would have enough context to distinguish between:

- A sequencer that is **genuinely stalled** (not making progress, something is wrong)
- A sequencer that is **correctly responding to a local-safe reorg** (unsafe head is behind because the EL was rewound to follow a corrected safe chain)

If the conductor can see that a local-safe reorg occurred — e.g. the safe/local-safe heads moved backwards while the sequencer's state is consistent with that new safe chain — it can determine that the sequencer is actually healthy and should continue sequencing from the rewound head, rather than stopping it.

## Additional Context

This issue was also observed on fresh devnet deployments: if a sequencer's op-node restarts and comes back with `sequencerEnabled=true, sequencerStopped=true`, the conductor won't re-activate it because the unsafe head is behind — the same circular deadlock pattern. The current workaround is manually calling `admin_startSequencer` with the current unsafe head hash.

topIssues.title: op-supervisor/op-supernode cross-safe cannot drain a backlog faster than real-time after a stall
topIssues.author: jelias2
topIssues.body:
## Summary

On a 2-chain interop network, after a multi-hour interruption the per-chain **local-safe** head and the batcher recover to the tip within seconds, but the **cross-safe** head (`l2_safe`, advanced by the interop verification activity in `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop`) falls far behind and **advances at exactly ~1 timestamp/s ≈ real-time**, so the gap never closes. Observed: ~21.6k blocks / **~12h behind**, holding constant.

This is confirmed to be inherent current behavior, not a single-node fault: **three independent supervisor replicas all sit at an identical 12.06h behind and advance at ~1/s.**

## Evidence

Steady-state metrics across three replicas (one was patched with an experimental fix, see "Ruled out"):

| replica | advance rate | wait rate | behind |
|---|---|---|---|
| control-0 | 0.98/s | 0.96/s | 12.06h |
| control-1 | 0.99/s | 0.93/s | 12.06h |
| patched   | 1.00/s | 2.77/s | 12.06h |

All advance cross-safe at ~1/s and remain ~12h behind. CPU was ~30% of a 1-core limit, memory flat — **not resource-bound**.

## Ruled out: the per-no-op backoff

PR #21116 (now closed) hypothesized the fixed 1s `backoffPeriod` after no-op verification rounds was the limiter and replaced it with a short catch-up backoff. The live A/B disproves it: the patched replica retried ~3× more often (2.77 vs ~0.95 waits/s) but produced **zero** extra advances and closed **none** of the gap. The 1s sleeps were a *symptom* of correctly waiting for the next timestamp to become verifiable — not the cause. See the closed PR for the full writeup.

## Where the real gate likely is

The rate-limiter is whatever bounds the verifiable frontier per round in `op-supernode/supernode/activity/interop`:

- `observeRound` → `checkChainsReady` → `OptimisticAt(ts)` readiness for already-local *past* timestamps,
- the per-round `SameL1Chain` L1-consistency checks (`l1Checker`), and/or
- a frontier ceiling tied to L1-origin progression.

**Signature to chase:** after advancing to timestamp `T`, `T+1` only becomes advanceable ~1s of wall-time later, regardless of how often it is retried. That time/data pacing is what must change for cross-safe to drain a backlog faster than real-time. The two chains run at 1s and 2s block times, so the 1s-granularity timeline interacts with per-chain block cadence — worth checking how `OptimisticAt`/readiness behaves for timestamps with no exact block on the slower chain.

## Impact

After any multi-hour stall, cross-safe (and therefore finalized) cannot recover promptly and effectively never catches up without manual intervention (DB reset / re-derive). Restarting the supervisor makes it worse (forces a full local-safe re-derivation of the backlog before verification resumes).

## Repro

1. Run a 2-chain interop devnet (op-supernode), ~1–2s block times, with cross-chain messages.
2. Stall cross-safe for several hours (e.g. wedge one sequencer EL) while unsafe keeps advancing, then restore.
3. After local-safe + batcher return to tip, observe `l2_safe`: it advances at ~1/s with idle CPU and the unsafe→safe gap stays roughly constant.

Diagnosed against op-supernode v0.3.1-rc.2.

topPRs.title: [codex] batcher consensus proof of concept
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This draft PR adds a blob-mode-only batcher consensus proof of concept.

- adds a rollup config verifier address and batcher proof endpoint wiring
- attaches proof calldata to blob batcher transactions without changing blob batch data
- verifies blob transaction calldata in op-node derivation via block-hash `eth_call` to an L1 verifier contract and skips invalid proofs
- adds verifier logs, metrics, and unit coverage for batcher, derivation, L1 client, and verifier helpers
- adds DevStack verifier and sidecar options, valid/invalid acceptance tests, OP Up demo mode, and `op-up smoke-batcher-consensus`
- adds a Rust proof sidecar that runs Commonware Simplex over a simulated 4-validator network and emits the resulting finalization certificate
- switches the Simplex certificate scheme to Commonware secp256r1 so the certificate signatures are EVM-checkable
- carries a `CWSIMPLX1 || digest || marker || fixed POC envelope || Commonware certificate` calldata envelope for the Commonware sidecar path
- verifies the Commonware Simplex finalization certificate in the DevStack L1 verifier by checking the proposal digest, signer bitmap, quorum signatures, and P256 signatures over `sha256(union_unique(finalize_namespace, proposal.encode()))`
- activates Osaka on the DevStack L1 preset used by the Commonware verifier so the L1 `eth_call` path has the P256 precompile available
- makes the OP Up batcher-consensus demo self-contained by using the no-fault-proofs single-chain preset and adding `--l2-rpc-port` for running valid and invalid demo networks side by side

## POC Caveat

The current sidecar runs a deterministic in-process Commonware Simplex network for the POC. The verifier now directly checks the Commonware secp256r1 certificate signatures in EVM, but the certificate layout and validator set are still fixed for this proof of concept rather than a production configurable committee/verifier contract.

## Validation

```bash
cargo test --manifest-path op-batcher-consensus-sidecar/Cargo.toml

go test ./op-service/batchconsensus ./op-devstack/sysgo -run 'TestBuild|TestBatchConsensusMockVerifier|TestBuildCommonware|TestBuildSigned' -count=1 -v

DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/batcher_consensus -run 'TestBatchConsensusValidProofAdvancesSafeHead' -count=1 -v

DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go test ./op-acceptance-tests/tests/batcher_consensus -run 'TestBatchConsensusInvalidProofDoesNotAdvanceSafeHead' -count=1 -v

go test ./op-up -run '^$'
go run ./op-up --help
go run ./op-up smoke-batcher-consensus all --help

# live OP Up demo smoke, with one shell per long-running devnet:
DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go run ./op-up --dir /tmp/op-up-batcher-consensus-valid --batcher-consensus-poc
DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth RUST_JIT_BUILD=1 go run ./op-up --dir /tmp/op-up-batcher-consensus-invalid --batcher-consensus-poc --batcher-consensus-poc-invalid --l2-rpc-port 8546
go run ./op-up smoke-batcher-consensus all

git diff --check
```

The DevStack acceptance tests show valid Commonware consensus proof calldata advancing `local-safe`, and invalid proof calldata being rejected with `false batch consensus verifier result` while `local-safe` remains at genesis.

The live OP Up smoke run started a valid proof demo on `http://localhost:8545` and an invalid proof demo on `http://localhost:8546`; `smoke-batcher-consensus all` observed the valid safe head reach the submitted transfer block and the invalid safe head stay below the submitted transfer block for 20 seconds.

Note: the DevStack and OP Up runs used `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-geth` in this environment because op-reth was not built locally.
